name: Jev context curation — 20-case pilot
description: Compare fresh answers to an unchanged user message using its original preceding chat history with versus without Jev whole-message omission/reordering.

scope.unit: one original target user message plus the complete original preceding history
scope.domain: research and supporting dialogue: investigating or understanding how something works
scope.selection: Coverage-first shortlist approved by the user; 2 cases per primary behavior category.
scope.self_contained: All 20 full prefixes, exact target messages, source identity, category definitions and review annotations are embedded. No sibling file is needed to reconstruct the inputs.

input_contract.baseline: Send case.input.history_messages in original order, then case.input.target_user_message, with the shared runner instructions.
input_contract.curator: Provide Jev the same original history and target user message. Jev selects/orders whole history-message IDs. Materialize original message objects in that order, then append the unchanged target.
input_contract.curator_message_id_mapping: case.source.history_message_ids is aligned one-to-one with case.input.history_messages; these IDs may be supplied to Jev.
input_contract.evaluation_session: Use a fresh isolated session for each case and condition; never feed one generated target answer into another case.
input_contract.label_isolation: Do not send the whole case JSON to either model. Categories, titles, selection reasons, evaluation_only, future/source answers and review notes are evaluator metadata, not prompt content.

pending_run_configuration.note: Deferred, not defaults. This file defines the cases; no evaluation or regeneration has run.

limitations: This is a pilot: cases share eight source conversations and overlapping histories. Split and analyze by conversation, not as 20 independent sessions.
Proposed dependency annotations and success criteria are unvalidated; no reference answers or finalized numeric grading rules have been authored.
Some cases require subject knowledge, external evidence or subjective rubrics. The dataset is not uniformly answerable from history alone.
Earlier assistant answers may be inaccurate or incomplete and remain unchanged. They are not factual gold.
Short-prefix cases test dependency handling, not long-context degradation. Token counts are estimates.

categories.name: New topic: discard the old task
categories.description: The target introduces a complete new task; carrying over the old topic is unnecessary.

categories.name: Same subject, self-contained request
categories.description: Shared vocabulary does not mean the earlier messages are needed.

categories.name: Implicit task: recover the missing operation
categories.description: A fragment becomes a meaningful task only when paired with earlier instructions.

categories.name: Local reference: find the specific referent
categories.description: The task is stated, but a particular command or setup is referenced indirectly.

categories.name: Persistent constraints: retain earlier requirements
categories.description: The latest request omits requirements that should continue to apply.

categories.name: Constraint revision: supersede an earlier state
categories.description: The new turn changes which instructions or clues should remain active.

categories.name: Return to an earlier thread
categories.description: Recover an older named topic instead of treating only the last exchange as relevant.

categories.name: Combine multiple parts of the history
categories.description: Several separated pieces are jointly relevant; a single recent exchange is insufficient.

categories.name: Failure recovery: retain what already went wrong
categories.description: Useful context includes attempted solutions and the user’s response to them.

categories.name: Evidence limits: know what the history does not establish
categories.description: Recover the claim being challenged without mistaking prior assistant assertions for verified evidence.

# Dataset Card for WildChat

## Note: a newer version with 4.8 million conversations and demographic information can be found [here](https://huggingface.co/datasets/allenai/WildChat-4.8M).

## Dataset Description
 
- **Paper:** https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.01470

- **Interactive Search Tool:** https://wildvisualizer.com ([paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.03753))

- **License:** [ODC-BY](https://opendatacommons.org/licenses/by/1-0/)

- **Language(s) (NLP):** multi-lingual

- **Point of Contact:** [Yuntian Deng](https://yuntiandeng.com/)

### Dataset Summary

WildChat is a collection of 650K conversations between human users and ChatGPT. We collected WildChat by offering online users free access to OpenAI's GPT-3.5 and GPT-4. The dataset contains a broad spectrum of user-chatbot interactions that are not previously covered by other instruction fine-tuning datasets: for example, interactions include ambiguous user requests, code-switching, topic-switching, political discussions, etc. WildChat can serve both as a dataset for instructional fine-tuning and as a valuable resource for studying user behaviors. Note that this version of the dataset only contains non-toxic user inputs/ChatGPT responses.

### Updates

**2024-10-17: Content Update.** Conversations flagged by [Niloofar Mireshghallah](https://homes.cs.washington.edu/~niloofar/) and her collaborators in ["Breaking News: Case Studies of Generative AI's Use in Journalism"](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.13706) for containing PII or sensitive information have been removed from this version of the dataset.

**2024-07-22: Content Update.** All toxic conversations identified by the OpenAI Moderations API or Detoxify have been removed from this version of the dataset.

**2024-06-26: License Change.** We have updated the license of WildChat to [ODC-BY](https://opendatacommons.org/licenses/by/1-0/). This change is retroactively applied to any previous downloads under the ImpACT license.

### Languages

66 languages were detected in WildChat.

### Personal and Sensitive Information

The data has been de-identified with Microsoft Presidio and hand-written rules by the authors.

### Data Fields

- `conversation_id` (string): Each conversation has a unique id.
- `model` (string): The underlying OpenAI model, such as gpt-3.5-turbo or gpt-4.
- `timestamp` (timestamp): The timestamp of the last turn in the conversation in UTC.
- `conversation` (list): A list of user/assistant utterances. Each utterance is a dictionary containing the `role` of the speaker (user or assistant), the `content` of the utterance, the detected `language` of the utterance, whether the content of the utterance is considered `toxic`, and whether PII has been detected and anonymized (`redacted`).
- `turn` (int): The number of turns in the conversation. A turn refers to one round of user-assistant interaction.
- `language` (string): The language of the conversation. Note that this is the most frequently detected language in the utterances of the conversation.
- `openai_moderation` (list): A list of OpenAI Moderation results. Each element in the list corresponds to one utterance in the conversation.
- `detoxify_moderation` (list): A list of Detoxify results. Each element in the list corresponds to one utterance in the conversation.
- `toxic` (bool): Whether this conversation contains any utterances considered to be toxic by either OpenAI Moderation or Detoxify.
- `redacted` (bool): Whether this conversation contains any utterances in which PII is detected and anonymized.

### Empty User Inputs

This dataset includes a small subset of conversations where users submitted empty inputs, sometimes leading to hallucinated responses from the assistant. This issue, first noticed by @yuchenlin, arises from the design of our Huggingface chatbot used for data collection, which did not restrict the submission of empty inputs. As a result, users could submit without entering any text, causing the assistant to generate responses without any user prompts. This occurs in a small fraction of the dataset---12,405 out of 652,139 conversations.
